full_judgment:
2. The appeal arose out of a suit, Title Suit No. 689 of 1976, brought by the first respondent in the Third Court of Munsif Jessore, for declaration of title to and confirmation of possession in certain land. The case of the plaintiff briefly, is that the land in suit belonged to one Pagal Rishi, Nimai Chand took lease of the said land, from Pagal Rishi by means of a registered patta dated 13 February, 1952. On the death of Nimai Chand the plaintiff who happens to be his only son got the property by way of inheritance. He has since been in possession of the said land. The defendants have no right, title or interest therein. But they managed to have the said land recorded in their names on the plea that they had purchased the same in a certificate case which is false. They also obtained a decree in respect of the property against his father when he was dead. The said decree is not binding on the plaintiff. Taking advantage of the wrong recording the defendants are now threatening to dispossess the plaintiff from the land in suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. They did not deny the ownership of Pagal Rishi but contended that the patta dated 13 February, 1952 in favour of the father of the plaintiff was not genuine and that it was also not acted upon. They further pleaded that defendant No. 1 purchased the land in suit in auction in Certificate Case No. KM 4105/1954-55 and that defendant No.1 also took delivery of its possession through court. It was also their case that defendant No.1 had sold a portion of the said land to defendant Nos. 2-3 who had since been in possession of the same and that defendant No.1 had obtained an ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 59 of 1962 in respect of the land in question. 

 4. The trial Court on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, held that the decree in Title Suit No. 59 of 1962 was not binding on the plaintiff as Nimai Chand had taken settlement of the disputed land from Pagal Rishi by virtue of the registered patta Exhibit-I, that the plaintiff had acquired title thereto being the sole heir of Nimai Chand, that the decree in Title Suit No. 59 of 1962 was not binding on the plaintiff, that the defendants failed to substantiate their claim" of auction purchase and also possession in the disputed land and that the plaintiff has been in possession of the said land on payment of rent. 

 5. The contesting defendants took an appeal being Title Appeal No. 30 of 1977 therefrom. The learned Additional District Judge, Jessore, however, found that the patta was not executed by Pagal Rishi and it was never acted upon and that the plaintiffs had never possessed the suit land at any time within a period of 12 years of filing of the suit while the defendants had been in possession of the disputed land on the basis of auction purchase. As a result the learned Additional District Judge came to the conclusion that the plaintiff had no right, title, interest and possession in the land in suit and that the suit was barred by limitation and adverse possession. In coming to its conclusion the learned Judge took the view that the certified copy of the registered patta was inadmissible in the absence of any explanation for non-production of the original and that there was a total absence of any rent receipts from the side of the plaintiff. The learned Additional District Judge accordingly reversed the decision of the trial Court, by judgment and decree dated 6 April, 1978. 

 9. It is true that in a second appeal findings of fact cannot be reversed unless those are vitiated by misreading of evidence or non-consideration of material evidence. In the present case important material evidence had been ignored. The certified copy of the registered patta was marked Exhibit-I without any objection from the side of the defendants. There is a to tall absence of any evidence that the patta in question was not acted upon. Rent receipts showing payment of rent from the side of the plaintiff were filed and marked Exhibit-2 series. But those were not taken into consideration upon an erroneous assumption that the same were never filed, although record shows that the said exhibits were taken back by the party. PW 4 prayed for execution and registration of the patta whereas his evidence was misread and it was held that the original patta was not executed by Pagal Rishi. The defendants did not file any sale certificate or writ of delivery of possession in support of their claim of purchase of and entry into the disputed land. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has correctly noticed that the lower appellate Court misread the evidence on record and failed to take note of the aforesaid material evidence in arriving at its findings of facts. We find no reason to interfere with the judgment of the High Court Division.
